title: How ZPC onboards and offboards EKS, AKS and GKE clusters, including private GKE and AKS local authentication

checks.do: ZPC cannot onboard EKS clusters with private-only endpoint access; for GKE the pages disagree.
The Kubernetes tab statuses and the private GKE statuses.
The ZPC IP addresses to remove from allowlists after offboarding.

cluster-statuses.statement: On the Cloud Accounts Kubernetes tab, cluster Status is Success (onboarded, metadata collected), Warning (onboarded but metadata for some services cannot be collected), Error (not onboarded yet), Suspended (onboarded but tenant license expired) or Failed (onboarded but cloud account deleted).

quotes: Success: The Kubernetes cluster has been onboarded and ZPC is collecting configuration metadata.
Warning : The Kubernetes cluster has been onboarded but is unable to collect metadata for some services.
Error: The Kubernetes cluster has not been onboarded yet.
Suspended: The Kubernetes cluster has been onboarded but the tenant license is expired.
Failed: The Kubernetes cluster has been onboarded but the cloud account is deleted.

suspended-failed-no-collection.statement: ZPC cannot collect configuration metadata for suspended or failed Kubernetes clusters.

quotes: ZPC cannot collect configuration metadata for suspended Kubernetes clusters.
ZPC cannot collect configuration metadata for failed Kubernetes clusters.

eks-scope.statement: ZPC's EKS onboarding covers public and hybrid clusters; its script updates the publicAccessCidr property of hybrid clusters with ZPC IP addresses, creates a cluster role binding in Kubernetes and creates an IAM identity mapping.

quotes: ZPC offers insight into your Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) public and hybrid clusters.
Updates the publicAccessCidr property of the hybrid (public and private) clusters with ZPC IP addresses.
Creates a cluster role binding within Kubernetes.
Creates an IAM identity mapping.

eks-prereqs.statement: EKS onboarding requires the AWS account to be onboarded, being a Kubernetes Cluster Admin, permission to update the aws-auth configmap in the kube-system namespace and to create, update and delete the cluster role and binding, and for hybrid clusters UpdateClusterConfig and DescribeCluster permissions.

quotes: Make sure the AWS cloud accounts that contain the clusters are onboarded to ZPC.
Make sure you are a Kubernetes Cluster Admin.
Update aws-auth configmap in the kube-system namespace.
Create, update, and delete the cluster role and the cluster role binding.
Have the following additional permissions for hybrid clusters:
UpdateClusterConfig
DescribeCluster

eks-private-only.statement: ZPC cannot onboard EKS clusters with private-only endpoint access, and needs the CloudShell IP address allowlisted when onboarding a public and private cluster.

quotes: ZPC cannot onboard clusters with private-only endpoint access. ZPC also needs you to allowlist your CloudShell IP address if you're onboarding a public and private cluster.
evidence.after: # Onboarding EKS Clusters in a Single AWS account

aks-scope.statement: ZPC's AKS onboarding covers public clusters; its script creates a cluster role and role binding with the service principal used for onboarding the Azure account and allowlists the ZPC IP addresses if authorized IP ranges are enabled.

quotes: ZPC offers insight into your Microsoft Azure Kubernetes public clusters.
Creates a cluster role and role binding with the service principal used for onboarding the Microsoft Azure account.
Allowlists the ZPC IP addresses if your Kubernetes cluster has authorized IP ranges enabled.

aks-prereqs.statement: AKS onboarding requires the Azure account to be onboarded, being a Kubernetes Cluster Admin, and, for Azure AD with Kubernetes RBAC, membership of the AAD group with the Cluster Admin Access role, or, for Azure AD with Azure RBAC, the Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Cluster Admin role.

quotes: Make sure the Microsoft Azure cloud accounts that contain the clusters are onboarded to ZPC.
Make sure you are a Kubernetes Cluster Admin.
Azure AD Authentication with Kubernetes RBAC: You need to be a part of the AAD group which has the Cluster Admin Access role.
Azure AD Authentication with Azure RBAC: You have the Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Cluster Admin role.

aks-local-auth.statement: For AKS clusters without Azure AD integration, ZPC authenticates with a certificate and a secret key: it generates a bash script and a secret key, the secret key is submitted while the script runs, and the script sends a verification certificate to ZPC.

quotes: If you have not enabled Azure AD integration for an AKS cluster, ZPC can use a certificate and a secret key to authenticate with the AKS cluster and collect configuration metadata.
When you select clusters to onboard, ZPC generates a bash script and a secret key.
You need to run the bash script on your Kubernetes clusters and submit the secret key when the bash script is running.
Sends a verification certificate to ZPC.

aks-secret-key.statement: The secret key for AKS local authentication must be saved because it is needed for subsequent AKS cluster onboarding, and regenerating it has no impact on already onboarded clusters.

quotes: You need to submit this secret key for subsequent AKS clusters onboarding.
Regenerating a key has no impact on already onboarded clusters.

aks-kubelet.statement: In AKS local-authentication onboarding, a Kubelet Collection toggle controls whether Kubelet configuration metadata is collected.

quotes: Kubelet Collection: Use the toggle to control whether Kubelet configuration metadata needs to be collected or not.

gke-scope.statement: For GKE, the ZPC script allowlists the ZPC IP address in the cluster's Control plane authorized networks property, and a public cluster with that property disabled is onboarded automatically.

quotes: The script allowlists the ZPC IP address in the GKE cluster's Control plane authorized networks property.
If the GKE cluster is public, and has the Control plane authorized networks property disabled, the cluster is automatically be onboarded on ZPC.

gke-prereqs.statement: GKE onboarding requires the Kubernetes Engine API enabled on the GCP service account project and the onboarded project, and the viewer role on the service account.

quotes: Make sure the Kubernetes Engine API is enabled on the GCP service account project and the onboarded project.
Make sure the service account has the viewer role to collect GKE configuration metadata.

gke-public-hybrid.statement: Selected public GKE clusters are onboarded automatically, while hybrid clusters need a bash script run on them; the page says ZPC cannot onboard clusters with private-only endpoint access, and needs the CloudShell IP allowlisted for a public and private cluster.

quotes: If you have selected public clusters, they are automatically onboarded to ZPC. Hybrid clusters require you to run a bash script on the clusters for ZPC to communicate and collect metadata.
ZPC cannot onboard clusters with private only endpoint access. ZPC also needs you to allowlist your CloudShell IP address if you're onboarding a public and private cluster.
evidence.after: 4. On the Cluster Selection page, you can view and search for the following GKE cluster details available on the selected GKE account:

pgke-agent.statement: ZPC cannot make inbound API requests into the control plane of a private GKE cluster, so it uses a lightweight agent deployed on the cluster that sends configuration metadata back; the agent typically uses 100MB to 300MB and up to 500MB of memory.

quotes: ZPC cannot make inbound API requests into the Kubernetes control plane to retrieve configuration details for private GKE clusters.
ZPC offers a lightweight agent that can be deployed on the GKE private cluster which has access to the Kubernetes API and sends configuration metadata back to ZPC.
The agent typically consumes 100MB to 300MB, and upto 500MB of memory to function.

pgke-firewall.statement: Private GKE onboarding requires ingress firewall rules for udp:53, tcp:53, tcp:22 and tcp:10250.

quotes: Ensure that the private GKE cluster has ingress firewall rules for the following protocols and ports enabled:
- udp:53
- tcp:53
- tcp:22

pgke-statuses.statement: For private GKE clusters, Status is Success (agent sending all required information), Pending (agent deployed but not yet connected), Warning (only partial data received) or Error (agent cannot connect or cannot send any information).

quotes: Success: The agent is sending all required information to ZPC.
Pending: The agent is deployed on your GKE cluster but has not connected to ZPC yet.
Warning: ZPC is receiving only partial data from the agent.
Error: The agent is unable to connect to ZPC or is able to connect but is unable to send any information to ZPC.

pgke-api-key.statement: ZPC generates a unique API key per private GKE cluster that cannot be viewed again; in Pending status the key can be regenerated or deactivated, and deactivating it stops ZPC collecting configuration metadata.

quotes: ZPC generates a unique API key for each private cluster you have chosen to onboard.
You cannot view the created API key for the GKE cluster again, but regenerate or deactivate the API key for each cluster in the "Pending" status.
Click Deactivate API Key to deactivate the API key. ZPC can no longer collect configuration metadata.

pgke-pending-success.statement: After Finish is clicked a private GKE cluster's status becomes Pending, and becomes Success when ZPC confirms the private-cluster onboarding on the GCP Cloud Console is completed; the CRD file can be downloaded for clusters in Pending status.

quotes: After you click Finish, the GKE cluster's status changes to "Pending".
When ZPC is able to confirm you have completed the GKE private cluster onboarding on the GCP Cloud Console, the GKE cluster's status changes to "Success".
You can download the CRD file for each private GKE cluster in the "Pending" status.

pgke-agent-commands.statement: The private GKE onboarding page includes the commands kubectl create ns zpc, kubectl create secret generic zpc-api-key-credentials and kubectl apply -f kubernetesagent.yaml; creating the operator requires the API key generated on ZPC.

quotes: kubectl create ns zpc
kubectl create secret generic zpc-api-key-credentials
kubectl apply -f kubernetesagent.yaml
Creating the ZPC operator on your GKE private cluster requires you to submit the API key generated on ZPC.

offboard-eks.statement: After offboarding an EKS cluster, ZPC's access is removed with eksctl delete iamidentitymapping, deleting the zpc-reader cluster role binding and the zpc-read-role cluster role; for hybrid clusters ZPC's three allowlisted IPs are also removed.

quotes: eksctl delete iamidentitymapping --arn <zscalerRoleARN>
kubectl delete clusterrolebindings zpc-reader
kubectl delete clusterrole zpc-read-role

offboard-aks.statement: After offboarding an AKS cluster, the Azure Kubernetes Service Cluster User Role assignment is deleted with az role assignment delete and ZPC's cluster role binding is deleted with kubectl delete clusterrolebindings.

quotes: Delete the Azure Kubernetes Service Cluster User Role:
az role assignment delete --assignee
Delete ZPC's cluster role binding:
kubectl delete clusterrolebindings zpc-reader-

offboard-gke.statement: If an offboarded GKE cluster had control plane authorized networks enabled, ZPC's allowlisted IPs 52.13.162.179/32, 52.12.66.25/32 and 34.212.243.119/32 must be removed.

gke-private-only.summary: The GKE onboarding page says ZPC cannot onboard clusters with private-only endpoint access, while the private GKE page onboards private GKE clusters with an agent.

positions.says: ZPC cannot onboard GKE clusters with private-only endpoint access.

quotes: ZPC cannot onboard clusters with private only endpoint access. ZPC also needs you to allowlist your CloudShell IP address if you're onboarding a public and private cluster.
evidence.after: 4. On the Cluster Selection page, you can view and search for the following GKE cluster details available on the selected GKE account:

positions.says: Private GKE clusters are onboarded using a lightweight agent deployed on the cluster.

quotes: ZPC offers a lightweight agent that can be deployed on the GKE private cluster which has access to the Kubernetes API and sends configuration metadata back to ZPC.

gke-private-only.impact: An answer on onboarding a private GKE cluster cannot rest on the GKE page alone; the private GKE page gives an agent route.

status-sets.title: How the Kubernetes status sets relate
status-sets.detail: The Cluster Selection pages give Success, Pending or Failure; the Kubernetes tab gives Success, Warning, Error, Suspended, Failed; the private-GKE page gives Success, Pending, Warning, Error. The relation between the sets is not stated.

pgke-agent-hosts.title: Whether the private GKE agent hosts are production endpoints
pgke-agent-hosts.detail: The operator install command uses hosts such as int.app.zscwp.io and int.api.zscwp.io and a fixed ECR account; whether these are production endpoints is not stated, so the command is not reported.
